topic: Universal response-alphabet Airy law for unrestricted multi-arm binary randomized experiments. For every fixed integer K>=3 and every fixed real contrast c in R^K with sum_a c_a=0, sum_a |c_a|=2, and at least three nonzero coordinates, nature chooses an arbitrary labelled n-by-K schedule of binary potential outcomes Y_i(a) in {0,1}. Before observing outcomes, the designer chooses any probability law on assignments Z in {1,...,K}^n, including dependent assignments; the estimator is any measurable function of the full assignment labels and observed outcomes. The target is tau_c=n^(-1) sum_i sum_a c_a Y_i(a), loss is squared error, and R_n(c) is the infimum over all such design-estimator pairs of the worst-schedule risk. With this normalization the accepted parent gives first-order value 1/n; define d_n(c)=1/n-R_n(c). Write S_c={a:c_a!=0}, s_c=(sign(c_a)) on S_c, v=s_c/2, T_c={0,1}^{S_c}, b_t=t-1/2 and theta_t=c^T t. For xi in R^{S_c}, define the finite response-alphabet gauge V_c(xi)=min{sum_{t in T_c} lambda_t theta_t^2: lambda_t>=0 and sum_t lambda_t b_t=xi}; define kappa(c)=V_c(v). Define C_A=inf over phi in H^1(R) with ||phi||_2=1 of integral_R {4|phi_prime(x)|^2+|x|phi(x)^2} dx, and Lambda_c=C_A kappa(c)^(2/3). Prove, for every fixed K and every c in the declared class, the unrestricted expansion R_n(c)=1/n-Lambda_c n^(-4/3)+o(n^(-4/3)), equivalently lim n^(4/3)d_n(c)=Lambda_c. The upper theorem must use the explicit independent allocation q*_a=|c_a|/2 on S_c and a total full-label nonlinear Airy estimator; the lower theorem must construct compatible finite-schedule priors proving the same coefficient uniformly against every dependent outcome-independent design and every randomized labelled-data estimator, including allocation faces with zero arm counts. Give, for every rational c and rational eta>0, a terminating certificate that returns N and exact rational/algebraic upper and lower risk witnesses whose normalized gap is <=eta for all n>=N; extend the mathematical coefficient and risk expansion to real c using explicit rational contrast bracketing and the accepted parent continuity modulus, without claiming a Turing evaluator for an unrepresented real. A theorem for one contrast, the already-proved fixed-q* expansion, another order bound, or numerical convergence alone does not satisfy the kernel. Consumer: Hammer et al. (1996), ACTG 175, compares four antiretroviral regimens. For a prospective ACTG-175-style fixed-horizon trial with a prespecified binary regimen-versus-average contrast, the theorem changes allocation and shrinkage away from procedures known to be only first-order minimax, and the certificate quantifies whether contrast-weighted independent assignment is genuinely second-order optimal. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A full-dimensional response tube with basis [v, basis of ker(cᵀ)] extends the prior exact-target Bayes argument to every fixed contrast. For positive active allocations, z_a=c_a/(q_a H(q)) is a convex combination of e_a/c_a, so nuisance coordinates remain bounded near every simplex face. The identity H(q)-4=4 sum_a (q_a-q*_a)^2/q_a+4(1-Q) controls exterior and inactive-arm allocations, while a missing active arm yields a target-changing direction with zero observed-likelihood information. Exact checks covered seven rational contrasts, 28 missing-arm directions and 49 positive-allocation cases, including mixed signs, repeated weights, zero subset sums and small coefficients. These checks validate finite geometry, not the asymptotic theorem; no external universal multi-arm closure was found. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently prove and make effective the general exact-target all-count Bayes inequality for the piecewise-polynomial tube, including weak integration by parts across sign cells and uniform local, exterior and zero-count remainder bounds. EARLY KILL TEST: For c=(1/3,2/3,-1/4,-3/4), verify the regression, variance decomposition and directional bounds on all 16 response types, then add an inactive arm; any failed target identity, uncovered allocation face, or unrestricted procedure beating C_A(11/36)^(2/3) kills the universal formula. open_problems.open_problem: For every fixed multi-arm binary contrast c with at least three active coordinates, does unrestricted joint minimax design-estimation risk satisfy R_n(c)=n^{-1}-C_A V_c(s_c/2)^{2/3}n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}), with independent allocation q_a=|c_a|/2 attaining the expansion against all dependent outcome-independent designs?

source_refs.claim: Proves the unrestricted binary two-arm risk expansion n^{-1}-C_A n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}) via Bernoulli assignment, nonlinear shrinkage, and least-favorable priors; no multi-arm result is given.
source_refs.author: Timothy Sudijono, Edgar Dobriban, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: Establishes independent randomization as minimax for bounded two-arm potential outcomes, including arbitrary measurable estimators, but does not treat multi-arm contrasts or the Airy coefficient.
source_refs.author: Peter Hull

source_refs.claim: Treats arbitrary contrasts under permutation-invariant superpopulation classes, but the joint optimum is restricted to linear estimators and complete randomization rather than bounded finite schedules and nonlinear second-order minimaxity.
source_refs.author: Yuehao Bai

source_refs.claim: Develops design-based estimators for multi-armed RCT contrasts, confirming the practical multi-arm target while leaving unrestricted joint minimax risk uncharacterized.
source_refs.author: Peter Z. Schochet
source_refs.venue: Journal of Educational and Behavioral Statistics

open_problems.why_unsolved: The two-arm reduction uses a scalar class-variable transformation whose conditional experiment is a shifted binomial and whose hardest boundary has a one-dimensional linear variance cusp. With three or more active arms, the finite response alphabet has 2^{|S_c|} types, the target direction has a multidimensional nuisance kernel, and arbitrary designs include zero-count allocation faces. Neither the two-arm symmetrization nor Bai's linear-estimator argument supplies a compatible least-favorable prior that makes assignment labels ancillary on every face. The presolve tube and finite checks supplied with the topic are therefore hypotheses only: they do not establish weak integration by parts across polyhedral sign cells or uniform local, exterior, and zero-count remainders.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A matching upper-and-lower asymptotic theorem with coefficient C_A V_c(s_c/2)^{2/3}, an explicit full-label nonlinear estimator under q_a=|c_a|/2, and finite-schedule Bayes lower bounds covering every dependent design and zero-count face.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves from joint design-estimator optimality to the practical failure of first-order minimax procedures and then to a sharp Airy correction, exactly the narrative needed for the multi-arm question.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Standard randomized-experiment procedures are only first-order minimax -> bounded binary schedules permit nonlinear shrinkage and a sharp second-order benchmark -> determine whether the same Airy mechanism survives an unrestricted multi-arm contrast.

method_exemplars.technique: Symmetrize the unrestricted procedure, reduce binary schedules to a finite experiment, expand the nonlinear shrinkage risk using a discrete Stein identity, and match it with discretized least-favorable Airy priors.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It proves the exact scalar special case of the requested expansion; the required transfer replaces the shifted-binomial experiment by the response-alphabet gauge and controls its nuisance coordinates.

method_exemplars.technique: Average procedures over coordinatewise treatment swaps, use Jensen reduction to an assignment-free transformed statistic, and solve the resulting finite minimax decision problem.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its unrestricted two-arm symmetrization is the nearest design-side argument for proving that independent allocation remains optimal beyond affine estimators.

method_exemplars.technique: Convert a second-order minimax problem into a positive-eigenfunction or Schrödinger variational problem and construct the corresponding asymptotically optimal shrinkage rule.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired coefficient is itself a ground-state energy; Levit supplies the general proof architecture connecting local risk expansions, least-favorable priors, and the eigenvalue.

open_problems.open_problem: For rational multi-arm contrasts c and rational tolerances eta>0, can the universal minimax expansion be made effective by a terminating procedure that certifies, for all n beyond an explicit N, exact rational or algebraic upper and lower risk witnesses whose normalized coefficient gap is at most eta?

source_refs.claim: Its finite reduced game and least-favorable prior can be computed for moderate n, but the asymptotic proof does not provide a uniform all-n exact certificate, even in the two-arm presentation.
source_refs.author: Timothy Sudijono, Edgar Dobriban, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: Derives sharp finite-population minimax lower bounds and exact independent-sampling optima under bounded outcomes and unbiasedness, illustrating finite certificates in a restricted estimator class.
source_refs.author: P. M. Aronow, Patrick Lopatto

source_refs.claim: Reduces unrestricted bounded two-arm design-estimation to a finite minimax problem, but does not certify a multi-arm asymptotic coefficient uniformly over all sufficiently large sample sizes.
source_refs.author: Peter Hull

open_problems.why_unsolved: Numerically solving each finite minimax game does not certify an infinite tail of sample sizes. Effectivity requires rational control of the response-type polytope, algebraic approximations to the Airy ground state, explicit discretization and tail errors, and uniform remainder bounds over positive allocations and every missing-active-arm face. Existing exact reductions establish finite optimization problems or asymptotic limits, but do not connect the two through a terminating proof-producing algorithm.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A proved algorithm taking rational (c,eta), returning N plus exact upper-procedure and finite-prior lower-risk witnesses, and verifying symbolically that their n^{4/3}-normalized gap is at most eta for every integer n>=N.

writing_exemplar.why: It cleanly separates exact finite decision-theoretic reduction from asymptotic implications, a useful framing for explaining why computability and uniform certification are additional contributions.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Bounded outcomes make the unrestricted design problem finite and structured -> finite minimax rules can be computed -> turn that structure into a rigorous all-large-n certificate for arbitrary rational multi-arm contrasts.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent finite-n minimax risk by a convex game over response counts and least-favorable priors, then bound the discrete-to-continuum Airy approximation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired certificate must expose exact versions of the same upper estimator and Bayes lower bound used to establish the asymptotic coefficient.

method_exemplars.technique: Use sharp worst-case inequalities over a bounded hyperrectangle, equality conditions, and explicit independent-inclusion allocations to obtain checkable risk witnesses.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It demonstrates how a design-based minimax result can retain exact finite arithmetic and witness-level attainability rather than only an asymptotic rate.

method_exemplars.technique: Control second-order minimax remainders through the ground-state solution of the associated Schrödinger problem.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Certified algebraic upper and lower Airy approximations require quantitative versions of the variational machinery underlying the limit constant.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one construct confidence intervals or randomization tests for a multi-arm nonlinear Airy minimax estimator that have uniform finite-population coverage for the weak null c^T\bar Y=theta while retaining the estimator's n^{-4/3} worst-risk improvement?

source_refs.claim: Explicitly identifies inference for the nonlinear minimax procedure as an important unresolved problem and suggests inversion of randomization tests for weak nulls.
source_refs.author: Timothy Sudijono, Edgar Dobriban, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: Develops studentized Fisher randomization tests that are asymptotically valid for weak null hypotheses under standard randomized-experiment statistics.
source_refs.author: Jason Wu, Peng Ding
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Extends randomization tests and conditional randomization procedures to multi-armed clinical trials, but not to minimax nonlinear shrinkage estimators.
source_refs.author: Yanying Wang, William F. Rosenberger

open_problems.why_unsolved: Weak-null randomization inference cannot impute every missing potential outcome, while the Airy estimator is nonlinear, biased by design, and may depend on random arm counts including empty faces. Existing studentization arguments are built around asymptotically linear contrast estimators; replacing them with nonlinear shrinkage requires a new randomization expansion or a least-favorable calibration that remains uniform over all binary schedules without erasing the second-order gain.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A test statistic and inversion rule with a theorem proving uniform level or coverage over all fixed binary schedules and all declared contrasts, together with a risk or expected-length result showing preservation of the Airy estimator's second-order advantage.

writing_exemplar.why: The paper itself motivates practical use of the nonlinear minimax rule and then isolates inference as the missing step.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Nonlinear shrinkage materially lowers worst-case MSE -> practical trials require uncertainty quantification, not only point risk -> develop weak-null randomization inference compatible with the minimax estimator.

method_exemplars.technique: Studentize a randomization statistic so the sharp-null permutation distribution asymptotically dominates its weak-null sampling distribution, then invert the tests.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly addresses weak-null validity under finite-population randomization; the new work must replace its asymptotically linear statistic by the Airy shrinkage functional.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct conservative variance estimators for general designs through potential-outcome imputation and observable contrast substitutions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The contrast approach may control random-count and multi-arm variance terms without separately imputing every missing potential outcome.

method_exemplars.technique: Condition randomization tests on the realized multi-arm allocation structure and handle multiple contrast hypotheses.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the destination-side multi-arm randomization machinery that the two-arm Airy paper lacks.

open_problems.open_problem: Under fixed baseline covariates and a named covariate-restricted class of binary potential-outcome schedules, what is the sharp second-order joint minimax design-estimator expansion for a prespecified multi-arm contrast, and when does covariate balancing replace contrast-weighted independent allocation?

source_refs.claim: Explicitly lists incorporation of measured baseline covariates as an unresolved route to improving efficiency and power for the nonlinear minimax procedure.
source_refs.author: Timothy Sudijono, Edgar Dobriban, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: Derives minimax-variance covariate-balancing designs for two-arm experiments while fixing the estimation target and working without bounded-outcome nonlinear second-order analysis.
source_refs.author: Nathan Kallus
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B

source_refs.claim: Characterizes minimax randomization and Neyman allocation under exact permutation or block invariance, leaving approximate invariance and unrestricted nonlinear bounded-outcome procedures open.
source_refs.author: Yuehao Bai

open_problems.why_unsolved: Covariates break the full unit-permutation symmetry that drives the response-count reduction. Existing balancing results optimize variance for prescribed estimator classes, while the Airy result jointly optimizes over every design and estimator under an unstructured bounded schedule. A sharp synthesis must state a concrete residual or smoothness class, determine whether its imbalance penalty enters at n^{-1}, n^{-4/3}, or another scale, and analyze a nuisance-dependent differential operator rather than the scalar Airy operator.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: For a specified covariate-indexed schedule class, a theorem identifying the jointly minimax design and nonlinear estimator and giving a sharp risk expansion whose coefficient explicitly separates response-alphabet curvature from covariate-imbalance geometry.

writing_exemplar.why: Its discussion presents covariate incorporation as the natural next step after establishing the no-covariate theoretical benchmark.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Unrestricted bounded schedules yield an Airy minimax benchmark -> measured prognostic covariates can reduce risk through design and analysis -> characterize how covariate geometry changes the sharp multi-arm benchmark.

method_exemplars.technique: Express worst-case variance through a covariate imbalance norm and construct mixed randomized allocations minimizing that norm.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the design-side geometry needed to replace unrestricted permutation symmetry with a concrete covariate-restricted adversarial class.

method_exemplars.technique: Average procedures over permutation or block groups and use convexity to establish minimax randomization and allocation results.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its block-invariance argument is the closest finite-sample bridge between covariate structure and a joint design-estimation game.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive second-order minimax risk from positive solutions of a problem-specific Schrödinger equation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once covariate imbalance creates nuisance directions, the desired coefficient should arise from a higher-dimensional or nuisance-dependent analogue of the Airy variational problem.

open_problems.open_problem: For bounded continuous multi-arm potential outcomes Y_i(a) in [L,U], is the unrestricted second-order minimax coefficient for a fixed contrast determined solely by the endpoint response alphabet and the scaled gauge (U-L)^2 V_c(s_c/2), or can interior response values change the coefficient?

source_refs.claim: Shows that in the two-arm case the unrestricted minimax risk over [L,U] is exactly (U-L)^2 times the binary minimax risk, using an additional Bernoulli randomization of transformed observations.
source_refs.author: Timothy Sudijono, Edgar Dobriban, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: Studies bounded, including nonbinary, two-arm potential outcomes and obtains independent randomization and nonlinear unrestricted minimax estimation, but no multi-arm contrast result.
source_refs.author: Peter Hull

source_refs.claim: Provides finite-population causal inference for arbitrary factorial contrasts with many treatment combinations, but does not derive bounded-outcome unrestricted minimax risk.
source_refs.author: Tirthankar Dasgupta, Natesh S. Pillai, Donald B. Rubin
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B

open_problems.why_unsolved: The two-arm interval result relies on a scalar transformation followed by artificial Bernoulli rounding whose expectation preserves the target and whose induced risk can be compared exactly. With multiple arms and a signed contrast, separate rounding can introduce a vector nuisance experiment and may not preserve the facewise least-favorable geometry that defines V_c. The literature search found bounded two-arm reductions and general multi-arm contrast inference, but no endpoint-reduction theorem for unrestricted multi-arm minimax design and nonlinear estimation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either an endpoint-reduction theorem proving R_n^{[L,U]}(c)=(U-L)^2R_n^{\{0,1\}}(c) and hence the scaled Airy expansion, or a finite K, contrast, and interior-valued schedule counterexample with a different second-order coefficient.

writing_exemplar.why: Its central motivation is that known response bounds fundamentally reverse conventional design advice, naturally setting up the question of whether only the endpoints matter with multiple arms.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Outcome bounds change the minimax-optimal design -> two-arm unrestricted risk can be reduced to endpoint schedules -> determine whether endpoint universality survives signed multi-arm contrasts.

method_exemplars.technique: Recenter and rescale bounded outcomes, Bernoulli-randomize transformed observations, and compare the resulting estimator's risk to the binary finite experiment.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the exact endpoint-reduction argument whose target preservation and risk contraction must be generalized to the multi-arm gauge.

method_exemplars.technique: Use midpoint-centered outcomes, treatment recentering, group symmetrization, and convex finite-game reduction for bounded response pairs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its proof handles the unrestricted estimator class for interval-valued outcomes and therefore supplies the nearest design-estimation machinery for testing endpoint sufficiency.

method_exemplars.technique: Identify the second-order coefficient through the ground state of the limiting differential operator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: If interior outcomes alter the local information geometry, this framework determines whether the limiting potential remains |x| or changes.

literature_map:
Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026, arXiv:2608.13822) give the closest anchor: unrestricted binary two-arm design-estimation, an exact finite reduction, and an Airy n^{-4/3} correction.
Hull (2026, arXiv:2608.09812) independently shows that bounded outcomes favor independent rather than complete randomization and extends the two-arm problem to arbitrary measurable estimators.
Bai (2023, Journal of Econometrics) proves minimax randomization and Neyman allocation under permutation invariance, including general contrasts, but within linear-estimator and superpopulation structure.
Kallus (2018, JRSSB; arXiv:1312.0531) supplies minimax covariate-balancing design geometry, while Kallus (2021, JRSSB) separates precision-optimal designs from designs supporting randomization inference.
Aronow and Lopatto (2026, arXiv:2605.20572) obtain sharp finite-population minimax results for bounded survey outcomes under unbiasedness, including independent inclusion and midpoint-differenced Horvitz-Thompson estimation.
Levit (1981, 1986, Theory of Probability and Its Applications) supplies the classical bridge from second-order minimax expansions to elliptic or Schrödinger ground-state problems.
Schochet (2018, Journal of Educational and Behavioral Statistics) develops finite-population estimators for multi-armed RCT contrasts but does not address unrestricted joint minimaxity.
Dasgupta, Pillai, and Rubin (2015, JRSSB) formalize finite-population causal contrasts for many treatment combinations, providing a multi-arm/factorial comparison point rather than a minimax solution.
Li and Ding (2017, JASA) prove finite-population CLTs for multiple treatment levels and vector outcomes; these support conventional asymptotic inference but not nonlinear Airy shrinkage.
Wu and Ding (2021, JASA; arXiv:1809.07419) establish studentized randomization tests for weak nulls, the nearest inference machinery for the nonlinear minimax procedure.
Chattopadhyay and Imbens (2024, arXiv:2409.12498) develop conservative Neymanian variance methods for general designs, including contrast-based constructions.
Wang and Rosenberger (2020, Statistics in Medicine) treat conditional randomization tests in multi-armed clinical trials but not minimax nonlinear estimators.
Kandiros, Harshaw, and Sävje (2026, arXiv:2608.04909) optimize unrestricted procedures under network interference only at the rate/bounds level, illustrating how quickly exact constants disappear outside SUTVA.
Hammer et al. (1996, NEJM, DOI 10.1056/NEJM199610103351501) provide the four-regimen ACTG 175 application anchor, where a prespecified regimen-versus-average contrast is substantively natural.
Across the search, no paper supplied a universal multi-arm response-alphabet Airy coefficient, all-allocation-face lower bound, or uniform exact rational certification of that coefficient.
